newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to dispatch team to discuss car policy.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to dispatch team to discuss car policy.

text.p: Indonesian Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo said on Tuesday the government would send a negotiating team to Japan, the United States, and Europe this week to discuss its controversial national car policy.
"I will send a team tomorrow to Japan, U.S., and Europe to discuss Indonesia's national car policy. We hope the car policy will not to be brought to the WTO panel," he told reporters.
Influential Indonesian tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan on Tuesday urged Japan to hold bilateral talks with Indonesia in a bid to resolve Tokyo's objection to the car policy.

"The only thing I can do is to tell the Japanese government not to be too short-sighted. We can discuss this matter in a bilateral way...so that it doesn't have to be brought to the WTO," he told Reuters.

Japan, the United States and the European Union have challenged the Indonesian policy at the World Trade Organisation, saying tax and tariff breaks granted to the Indonesian and South Korean companies involved contravene free trade regulations.
A company controlled by President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra has been picked by the government to produce the national car in a joint-venture with South Korea's Kia Motors Corp.
Ariwibowo said the government had no plans to give the same privileges to any other company except Mandala Putra's PT Timor Putra Nasional.
Other companies, including a joint venture between another Suharto son Bambang Trihatmodjo and Hyundai Motor of South Korea, have sought similar tax breaks.

"The Japanese car industry is not worried over the national car. I think it's just the bureaucracy," said Hasan, who held talks late last week in Tokyo with executives from Toyota Motor Corp over the Indonesian car policy.
Toyota has an 8.26 percent stake in Indonesia's top automobile maker Astra International. Hasan was last week elected Astra's president-commissioner.
As of February 3, the Nusamba group, which is headed by Hasan, owned an 8.83-percent stake in Astra, making it the third largest shareholder.
The Nusamba group is 80-percent owned by three charitable foundations headed by Suharto and 10-percent each by Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto.

Nusamba has 50-percent stakes in two Indonesian companies which have a combined 30-percent stake in the huge Busang gold property in East Kalimantan province. The deposit it estimated to contain gold currently worth $24 billion.
"I think the Japanese government will understand. Indonesia is a bigger market than Germany, France and England put together," said Hasan, who regularly plays golf with Suharto.
"So (do) they (Japan) want to have the market or (do) they want to lose the market?," he said.
"If they are smart, they will go with us," he added.
